title: Introduction to Synchronization and Replication in 4D v12
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Integrated data-engine REPLICATE and SYNCHRONIZE commands
Replication metadata (stamps, IDs, CRUD action tracking)
REMOTE vs. LOCAL data connection contexts

historical_commentary.text: 4D v12's built-in REPLICATE/SYNCHRONIZE data-engine mechanism described here was a significant improvement over prior ad hoc approaches (SOAP, 4D Open, import/export) and its core CRUD-metadata-and-conflict-resolution model has remained part of 4D's classic feature set. It is still relevant for classic-language 4D applications needing offline/mirror/satellite database scenarios, though modern mobile and distributed-data architectures increasingly favor REST/ORDA-based data access with client-side caching or dedicated sync services rather than 4D's native replication engine for new greenfield projects.
related_updates: REST APIs built on ORDA (introduced v16 R5/17+) are now often used for building distributed/offline-capable clients instead of native REPLICATE/SYNCHRONIZE
4D's native replication/synchronization commands have continued to be maintained and refined in versions since v12
